children.text: Snell's Law

At a dielectric interface, \(n_1\sin\phi_1=n_2\sin\phi_2\), with angles measured from its normal. Light travels at speed \(c/n\). Use geometrical optics and the original diagrams. Part A concerns a semicircular block in air. Part B concerns a cylindrical rod of index \(n_1=1.50\), surrounded by index \(n_2=1.00\), with an entry polymer of index \(n_3=1.40\). Part C concerns meridional rays in an optical fibre.

statement.text:
Snell's Law
At a dielectric interface, \(n_1\sin\phi_1=n_2\sin\phi_2\), with angles measured from its normal. Light travels at speed \(c/n\). Use geometrical optics and the original diagrams. Part A concerns a semicircular block in air. Part B concerns a cylindrical rod of index \(n_1=1.50\), surrounded by index \(n_2=1.00\), with an entry polymer of index \(n_3=1.40\). Part C concerns meridional rays in an optical fibre.

A.1. Two colours

Rays a and b enter a semicircular block radially and leave its flat bottom with refraction angles \(\theta_a<\theta_b\). Which ray travels faster inside? Explain.
A.2. Index difference
As internal incidence increases, ray b ceases to exit at \(45^\circ\), and a at \(50^\circ\). Find \(n_b-n_a\).
B.1. Return to the polymer

Light enters the rod from the polymer at angle \(\theta\) to its axis. Determine the incident-angle range for total reflection at both the side and far end, returning light to the polymer.
B.2.i. Oil at the far end
What happens if the far end is coated with a thick oil layer of index 1.60?
B.2.ii. Immersion in water
For the original rod without oil, what happens in water of index 1.33?
C.1. Straight-fibre acceptance

A fibre core of index \(n_1\) is surrounded by cladding of index \(n_2<n_1\). External medium has index \(n_3\). Find maximum acceptance angle \(\theta_a\).
C.2. Bent-fibre acceptance
The core diameter is \(50\,\mu\mathrm m\) and the minimum bend radius of its centreline is 1.0 cm. Derive the altered acceptance angle for the limiting meridional ray.
C.3. Acceptance angles in air
For \(n_1=1.45,n_2=1.44,n_3=1\), find both acceptance angles using C.1 and C.2.

children.text: Snell's Law
A.1. Two colours
At the common internal incidence angle, Snell gives \(n_a<n_b\). Thus \(c/n_a>c/n_b\), so ray a travels faster.
A.2. Index difference
At critical incidence \(n\sin\theta_c=1\). Therefore \(n_b-n_a=1/\sin45^\circ-1/\sin50^\circ=0.1088\).
B.1. Return to the polymer

If the rod angle is \(\theta_1\), side reflection requires \(\cos\theta_1>n_2/n_1\), whereas far-end reflection requires \(\sin\theta_1>n_2/n_1\). Using \(n_3\sin\theta=n_1\sin\theta_1\), \[\arcsin(n_2/n_3)<\theta<\arcsin(\sqrt{n_1^2-n_2^2}/n_3).\] Numerically \(45.58^\circ<\theta<53.00^\circ\).
B.2.i. Oil at the far end
The far-end medium has index greater than the rod. Total internal reflection there is impossible. No incident-angle interval returns all the light to the polymer.
B.2.ii. Immersion in water

Side reflection requires \(\theta_1<\arccos(1.33/1.50)=27.54^\circ\), while far-end reflection requires \(\theta_1>\arcsin(1.33/1.50)=62.46^\circ\). These intervals do not intersect, so no total-return interval exists.
C.1. Straight-fibre acceptance

At the side-wall critical angle, the core angle to the axis satisfies \(\sin\theta_{\rm core}=\sqrt{n_1^2-n_2^2}/n_1\). Entry refraction gives \[\sin\theta_a=\frac{\sqrt{n_1^2-n_2^2}}{n_3}.\] If this exceeds one, all physical entry angles are accepted.
C.2. Bent-fibre acceptance

Let \(a=25\,\mu\mathrm m\), bend radius \(R=10000\,\mu\mathrm m\). Conservation of the ray impact parameter between inner and outer core radii requires \(\sin\phi_{\rm inner}=(R+a)\sin\phi_{\rm outer}/(R-a)\). Set \(\sin\phi_{\rm outer}=n_2/n_1\). Entry refraction then gives \[\sin\theta_{a,\rm bend}=\frac1{n_3}\sqrt{n_1^2-n_2^2\left(\frac{R+a}{R-a}\right)^2}.\] It is smaller than the straight value. If the radicand is negative, the limiting inner-edge ray cannot be guided.
C.3. Acceptance angles in air

The straight acceptance is \(\arcsin\sqrt{1.45^2-1.44^2}=9.79^\circ\). The bent result is \(\arcsin\sqrt{1.45^2-1.44^2(10025/9975)^2}=5.15^\circ\), about \(4.64^\circ\) less. Use the centreline-radius convention of the source.
